articles.text:
This lesson discusses Spanish pronunciation, particularly weak-stressed vowels. 
In Spanish, vowels maintain their sound regardless of stress, but when they occur in unstressed syllables (weak stress), English speakers often have difficulty distinguishing them because English rarely contrasts vowel quality in unstressed positions. 
Practising minimal pairs—pairs of words differing only in their weak-stressed vowel—helps learners overcome this issue. 
Understanding the rhythmic difference between Spanish and English is also crucial: whereas English lengthens stressed syllables and shortens others, Spanish rhythm keeps syllables more evenly timed. 
Mastering these patterns involves extensive practice with contrasting pairs and sometimes with nonsensical syllables to focus solely on pronunciation.
